angle: Translate "AI changes jobs" into task-level redesign, metrics, and reskilling plans leaders can execute
sourceTitle: AI Is Changing Jobs, Not Eliminating Them
linkedinPost:
Most AI misses start with the wrong unit of change: jobs instead of tasks.

Knowledge at Wharton highlights a key point: AI is changing jobs by automating slices of work, not erasing entire roles. That matches what I see in the field — value shows up when we redesign workflows task-by-task, metric-by-metric.

My playbook in enterprises:

- Start with a task inventory, not an org chart. Map 30–50 recurring tasks in a role and score for volume, variability, and risk.

- Automate the boring 20% that blocks throughput, then reinvest the saved minutes into higher-value tasks you’ve already identified (don’t just “give time back” — assign it).

- Measure at the task level: handle time, first-pass yield, rework rate, and deflection. If you can’t move those, you won’t see ROI on the P&L.

A recent Wharton piece frames this shift well. In my experience, teams that ship small task wins weekly compound adoption and trust; teams that chase “AI job replacement” stall.

Question: What’s one task in your team you’d confidently automate to 80% — and what would you do with the freed capacity? #AITransformation #AIStrategy #EnterpriseAI
